subject: Smallest source-bound RCC controlled-inspection architecture; proposal only
scope: Read-only source analysis and proposal; no implementation, real metadata inspection, compiler advancement or publication
decision: GO bounded architecture proposal; HOLD execution/compiler admission until explicit source-bound implementation and gates
proposal:
Propose one private controlled-inspection orchestrator beside the private compiler, with a frozen observation value and an injected bounded runner. Keep the compiler pure. The first supported input is one harness-owned Linux v2 fixture with an exact complete path and action declaration; do not broaden it to arbitrary package authorization or cross-platform source capture.

1. Own a fresh operation directory, source/destination directory descriptors, and a separate output directory. Use source_staging.stage_selected_files to produce the exact measured selected bytes in an empty owner-private staged directory. Protected environment inputs and action files must be in the complete declaration. Disable bytecode generation and ambient host PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/user-site influence; external Python paths are outside this first profile. Re-measure the staged selection and enforce the exact complete fixture inventory before preparation and after metadata execution. Compare bytes, normalized modes and path inventory; reject additions, deletions or mutation. Owner-private staging is not a sandbox against package code or hostile same-UID writers.

2. Select the pinned RCC executable and verify its version through the bounded runner. Call prepare_runtime_for_inspection with the staged package.yaml, caller identity and a source generation derived from the measured inventory, retaining the exact same-publish specification/artifact pair and provider-bound descriptor. Inject the bounded runner into preparation; do not use its default subprocess.run capture/timeout as the future supervisor. Preserve the existing cache policy: a cache hit can reuse the pair without acquire and supplies no fresh availability proof. Require the current env-exec receipt for the actual execution, or explicitly request current acquire evidence under the same provider when the acceptance claim requires it. Never publish a second time solely to obtain a specification digest.

3. Build the metadata command using build_exec_command with the exact prepared descriptor/provider and a fresh receipt path. Reuse the Actions CLI metadata format, not the database/import_service lifecycle. Run python metadata collection in the staged working directory. Store metadata in the operation output directory, not inside selected source; use an explicit launcher only to redirect metadata output. It must call the installed Core CLI and record interpreter/Core distribution origin and version so a host checkout overlay cannot masquerade as the prepared environment. Avoid the legacy robocorp fallback for this controlled v2 profile. Metadata discovery imports package code; it is execution, with no hostile-code isolation claim.

4. The runner owns Popen and RccProcessHandle. Drain stdout/stderr concurrently with explicit byte caps and one monotonic execution deadline covering version, preparation, acquisition when needed, and metadata. Cap metadata and receipt reads before JSON parsing; reuse the compiler's 1MiB metadata/1000-action bounds and require a declared diagnostics/receipt policy. On limit, timeout, cancellation, exceptions and ordinary exit, capture observed descendants before owner shutdown and use force_kill_until with a reserved cleanup deadline. Record wrapper reaping, snapshot completeness, live descendants, zombies and errors separately. Require descendant_reap_complete for a successful controlled observation. A point-in-time process snapshot cannot guarantee hostile fork containment; incomplete observation is HOLD, never cleanup success. Remove only operation-owned paths after process cleanup; record unknown or refused cleanup instead of deleting shared caches or original source.

5. Read the RCC receipt through read_receipt after the bounded read; bind artifactDigest, valid verification and leaseId to this invocation, same provider, command, return code, source inventory and metadata digest. The existing receipt verifier checks only artifact/verification/lease fields, so the new observation must additionally carry its actual launch context. Reject malformed/oversized metadata and map each returned file/name exactly once to a harness-declared capability in the staged source. Reject outside-root paths, missing/extra/duplicate actions and mismatched declarations. Convert validated metadata into SuppliedActionMetadata and the retained pair into SuppliedRccIdentity only at the pure compiler boundary.

6. Feed the same pre/post-verified source bytes, measured inventory, declaration and metadata to compile_controlled_fixture. Keep its ProposedControlledCompilation.inspection_status='not_run' unchanged: it remains the pure supplied-input proposal. Return a separate bounded inspection observation beside that proposal; do not relabel the compiler result, admit a Package Revision, persist a descriptor, publish artifacts, change Runtime/database state or promote an environment cache entry into durable authority. Inspection acceptance requires the distinct observed execution/source/cleanup receipt, not the compiler's deterministic bytes alone.

Smallest new surface: one private orchestration module, one immutable observation type, a bounded runner implementing the existing Runner seam for version/publish/acquire, and the existing RccProcessHandle for env-exec. Reuse adapter parsing/provider validation/cache, Linux staging/measurement, process cleanup and pure compiler validation. Extract only a small metadata-command builder if needed; importing the existing import_service would pull Runtime/database hooks and its unbounded communicate()/source-tree metadata file behavior into the new boundary.

Required gates before implementation acceptance: deterministic declared fixture success with actual pinned RCC and receipt; same environment/new source cache reuse with a new execution/source observation; provider context preserved; stale cached artifact/current exec failure handled without invented availability; source mutation/addition/deletion rejected; outside/duplicate/missing metadata rejected; oversized output/metadata/receipt stops within policy; timeout/cancel/descendant survival/zombie/incomplete snapshot remain failures with recorded cleanup; no DB/publisher/shared-cache writes; no input source mutation. Use focused tests and one real controlled execution, not the full Runtime or renderer acceptance suites.

source_evidence._rcc_runtime_adapter.py: prepare_runtime_for_inspection retains same-publish pair; cache can reuse pair without acquire; Runner injection exists. build_exec_command preserves provider; RccProcessHandle exposes capture_owned_processes/force_kill_until. read_receipt checks artifact/validverification/lease. Default runner captures unbounded output and direct-child timeout.
source_evidence._actions_import.py: Existing CLI metadata command is reusable format; existing implementation writes metadata within import_path, communicate has no timeout, and import_service touches DB/Runtime hooks.
source_evidence.deployments/source_staging.py: Linux caller-owned descriptors, private empty destination, no-follow identity staging, complete selected-source inventory; failure cleanup only observed owned entries; caller owns successful stage cleanup.
source_evidence._common/process.py: Cleanup separates wrapper/live/zombie/errors/snapshotcompleteness and descendant_reap_complete. Point-in-time snapshots do not provide hostile process containment.
source_evidence.01ca package_compiler.py: Pure supplied metadata/RCC pair; exact declaration/source agreement; 1MiB metadata,1000actions,64MiBsource/archive; immutable proposal inspection_status Literal not_run.

doc_proposal.delta: A controlled RCC metadata inspection must bind one declared staged source inventory before and after execution to the same-publish specification/artifact pair, provider-bound env-exec command, verified execution receipt, bounded metadata output, and observed process cleanup. Preparation cache reuse does not prove current artifact availability or metadata execution. Keep metadata output outside selected source and reject source mutation or an action path/name outside the exact fixture declaration. Reuse the adapter, Linux staging and owned process lifecycle without invoking Runtime database/import hooks. The pure compiler still reports supplied-input inspection as not run; an actual inspection receipt is separate evidence, and neither value establishes Package Revision admission, authorization, hostile-code isolation, or publication.
doc_proposal.evidence: Verified exact7eca preparation/cache/runner/receipt and existing staging/lifecycle seams; exact01ca compiler explicitly accepts supplied inputs and reports not_run.
doc_proposal.uncertainty: Deadline/output policies, exact env-exec receipt surface and metadata launcher/process ownership require implementation and actual controlled execution. No new inspection was run.
